name: Inclusion Body Myositis

ethnicAssociations: Most common inflammatory myopathy in patients over 50
Less commonly reported in Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ENMC 2011 Clinically Defined / Lloyd et al. 2014 Criteria

criteria.description: Finger flexor weakness (FDP) greater than or equal to shoulder abduction weakness
Quadriceps weakness greater than or equal to hip flexor weakness
Muscle biopsy with endomysial inflammatory infiltrate, rimmed vacuoles, protein aggregates, or mitochondrial pathology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinicopathologically defined: characteristic clinical pattern (finger flexor and quadriceps weakness) plus pathognomonic biopsy features. Clinically defined: characteristic weakness pattern in age >45 with duration >12 months.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: IBM is commonly misdiagnosed as polymyositis. Key difference: IBM does not respond to immunosuppressive therapy. Anti-cN1A antibodies have ~60-70% sensitivity and ~90% specificity.

pathognomonic.notes: Asymmetric finger flexor weakness; difficulty gripping; the most distinguishing clinical feature
Knee buckling, difficulty rising from chairs, falls; often asymmetric
Side-to-side asymmetry distinguishes from other myopathies

common.symptomName: Difficulty with grip (opening jars, turning keys)
common.notes: From finger flexor weakness; early functional impairment
From quadriceps weakness causing knee buckling
Present in ~40-60%; may require cricopharyngeal myotomy

laboratory: CK mildly to moderately elevated (typically 1-12x normal; often <10x ULN)
imaging: MRI muscle: fatty infiltration and atrophy of quadriceps, forearm flexors
MRI: asymmetric pattern of muscle involvement
MRI: relative sparing of rectus femoris compared to vastus muscles
Ultrasound: increased echogenicity in affected muscles
genetic: No causative gene for sporadic IBM
Hereditary IBM (hIBM/GNE myopathy) is a separate entity caused by GNE gene mutations
SQSTM1, VCP mutations cause IBM-like pathology in familial cases
other: EMG: mixed myopathic and neurogenic features (short- and long-duration MUPs)
Muscle biopsy: endomysial inflammatory infiltrate (CD8+ T cells invading non-necrotic fibers)
Muscle biopsy: rimmed vacuoles with basophilic granular inclusions
Muscle biopsy: congophilic amyloid deposits, p62 and TDP-43 aggregates

distinguishingFeatures: MG has fatigable weakness without atrophy
MG has positive AChR or MuSK antibodies
MG does not have elevated CK
ALS has upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia)
ALS EMG shows active denervation without myopathic features
IBM is frequently misdiagnosed as treatment-refractory polymyositis

redFlags: Treatment-resistant polymyositis should prompt reconsideration as IBM
IBM does NOT respond to conventional immunosuppressive therapy (steroids, methotrexate, IVIg)
Dysphagia can cause aspiration pneumonia and significant morbidity
Average 10-15 year disease course to wheelchair dependence
Anti-cN1A antibodies are also found in Sjogren syndrome and SLE; clinical context essential
Hereditary inclusion body myopathy (GNE myopathy) spares quadriceps, unlike sporadic IBM
references: Rose MR; ENMC IBM Working Group. 188th ENMC International Workshop: Inclusion Body Myositis. Neuromuscul Disord. 2013;23(12):1044-1055.
Greenberg SA. Inclusion body myositis: clinical features and pathogenesis. Nat Rev Rheumatol. 2019;15(5):257-272.
Lloyd TE, et al. Evaluation and construction of diagnostic criteria for inclusion body myositis. Neurology. 2014;83(5):426-433.
